title: “One who has cut off craving, Without remainder, Dried up the swift stream — That monk abandons the near and far shore, Like a serpent…
content:
“One who has cut off craving,
Without remainder,
Dried up the swift stream —
That monk abandons the near and far shore,
Like a serpent sheds its worn-out skin.”

“One who has destroyed conceit,
Without remainder,
As a great flood destroys a fragile reed —
That monk abandons the near and far shore,
Like a serpent sheds its worn-out skin.”

title: Elder Nun Mother of Vaḍḍha: Vaḍḍha, never fall into the realm of sensual desire. My son, do not share In repeated suffering. Blissful is the…
content:
Elder Nun Mother of Vaḍḍha:

Vaḍḍha, never fall into the realm of sensual desire.
My son, do not share
In repeated suffering.

Blissful is the sage,
Without desire, with doubt cut off,
Cooled, self-controlled,
Without any defilements.

That sage practices
The path leading to right view,
Putting an end to suffering.
Vaḍḍha, strive on!

With confidence, mother spoke
This purpose for you —
“My dear mother! I think
That you have no sensual desire.”

“Vaḍḍha, whatever conduct —
Low, high, or middling —
Not even a little sensual desire
Exists in me.

I have destroyed all defilements,
Not heedless, meditating.
The three true knowledges are attained —
The Buddha’s instruction is done.”

Wonderful, my mother,
Encouraging and urging me,
With verses of truth,
Out of compassion.

Hearing my mother’s words,
Her motherly instruction,
I practiced the Dhamma gratefully,
Attaining security from bondage.

I am energetic, striving,
Day and night not lazy.
Well encouraged by my mother,
I attained the supreme purity.

title: “Monks, if a monk has a mind that is dispassionate and liberated regarding the form element, not grasping the defilements; regarding the feeling element ……
content: “Monks, if a monk has a mind that is dispassionate and liberated regarding the form element, not grasping the defilements; regarding the feeling element … perception element … formation element … consciousness element, he has a mind that is dispassionate and liberated, not grasping the defilements. Being liberated, he is firmly established. Being firmly established, he is content. Being content, he is not agitated. Being not agitated, he personally attains Nibbāna. He knows: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.’”

title: “The four right efforts: Here, venerable sirs, a monk awakens desire, makes effort, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives for the non-arising of unarisen…
content: “The four right efforts: Here, venerable sirs, a monk awakens desire, makes effort, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome states. He awakens desire, makes effort, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives for the abandoning of arisen evil, unwholesome states. He awakens desire, makes effort, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives for the arising of unarisen wholesome states. He awakens desire, makes effort, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives for the continuance, non-disappearance, strengthening, increase, development, and fulfillment of arisen wholesome states.”

title: “And what, monks, is the Dhamma leading to the full understanding of all clinging? Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises. The meeting of…
content: “And what, monks, is the Dhamma leading to the full understanding of all clinging? Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is contact. With contact as condition, feeling. Seeing thus, a well-taught noble disciple becomes disenchanted with the eye, with forms, with eye-consciousness, with eye-contact, with feeling. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. By being liberated, he knows: ‘I have fully understood clinging.’ Dependent on the ear and sounds … on the nose and odors … on the tongue and tastes … on the body and touches … Dependent on the mind and phenomena, mind-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is contact. With contact as condition, feeling. Seeing thus, a well-taught noble disciple becomes disenchanted with the mind, with phenomena, with mind-consciousness, with mind-contact, with feeling. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. By being liberated, he knows: ‘I have fully understood clinging.’ This, monks, is the Dhamma leading to the full understanding of all clinging.”

title: “Like a pit of filth Accumulated for many years — So too, a defiled person Is very hard to cleanse. Monks, know such a person…
content:
“Like a pit of filth
Accumulated for many years —
So too, a defiled person
Is very hard to cleanse.

Monks, know such a person —
Attached to households,
With evil desires, evil intentions,
Evil conduct, evil practices.

All of you, being of one mind,
Should shun such a person.
Blow him away like dust,
Throw him out like rubbish.

Expel the verbose one,
The fake ascetic.
Having expelled evil desires,
Evil conduct, evil practices —

Keep yourselves pure,
Live with the pure,
Mindful, dwelling together,
Wise, and make an end of suffering.”

title: “Monks, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye—desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. Sounds cognizable…
content: “Monks, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye—desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. Sounds cognizable by the ear … Odors cognizable by the nose … Tastes cognizable by the tongue … Tangibles cognizable by the body—desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. These, monks, are the five strands of sensual pleasure. The pleasure and joy that arise dependent on these five strands of sensual pleasure—this is called sensual pleasure, defiled pleasure, worldling’s pleasure, ignoble pleasure. ‘I say that this kind of pleasure should not be pursued, should not be developed, should not be cultivated, should be feared.’”

title: “Monks, defilement is a disease; defilement is a boil; defilement is a dart. Therefore, monks, the Tathāgata dwells without defilement, free from the dart. Therefore,…
content: “Monks, defilement is a disease; defilement is a boil; defilement is a dart. Therefore, monks, the Tathāgata dwells without defilement, free from the dart. Therefore, monks, if any monk has a wish, let him wish to dwell without defilement, free from the dart. Do not conceive about the eye, do not conceive in the eye, do not conceive from the eye, do not conceive ‘the eye is mine.’ Do not conceive about forms … Do not conceive about eye-consciousness … Do not conceive about eye-contact … Whatever feeling arises dependent on eye-contact … do not conceive about that feeling, do not conceive in it, do not conceive from it, do not conceive ‘that feeling is mine.’ Do not conceive about everything, do not conceive in everything, do not conceive from everything, do not conceive ‘everything is mine.’ Not conceiving thus, he does not cling to anything in the world. Not clinging, he is not agitated. Not agitated, he personally attains Nibbāna. He knows: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.’”

title: “And how, monks, is a monk one who sees sensual pleasures? When sensual pleasures are seen, then desire, lust for sensual pleasure, infatuation with sensual…
content: “And how, monks, is a monk one who sees sensual pleasures? When sensual pleasures are seen, then desire, lust for sensual pleasure, infatuation with sensual pleasure, and fever of sensual pleasure have no underlying tendency regarding sensual pleasures. Suppose, monks, there is a pit of glowing embers deeper than a man’s height, filled with glowing embers that are neither flaming nor smoking. Then a man comes who desires to live, not to die, who desires happiness and loathes suffering. Two strong men grab him by both arms and drag him toward that pit. He twists his body this way and that. Why? Because he knows: ‘I will fall into this pit of embers. Because of this, I will meet death or deadly suffering.’ So too, monks, a monk sees sensual pleasures as a pit of embers. And one who sees sensual pleasures thus has no desire, lust, infatuation, or fever for sensual pleasures as an underlying tendency.”

title: “Monks, these three are inner stains, inner enemies, inner foes, inner murderers, inner adversaries. What three? Greed, monks, is an inner stain, inner enemy, inner…
content: “Monks, these three are inner stains, inner enemies, inner foes, inner murderers, inner adversaries. What three? Greed, monks, is an inner stain, inner enemy, inner foe, inner murderer, inner adversary. Hatred, monks, is an inner stain … Delusion, monks, is an inner stain, inner enemy, inner foe, inner murderer, inner adversary. These, monks, are the three inner stains, inner enemies, inner foes, inner murderers, inner adversaries.”
